newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Urban Realty drops 260-has estate project.
newsitem.headline: Urban Realty drops 260-has estate project.

text.p: Urbancorp Realty Developers Inc (URDI) had shelved its plan to develop a 260-hectare industrial estate in an industrial township, south of Manila, URDI chairman Teodoro Borlongan said on Thursday.

Borlongan told reporters the decision was taken because of the removal of a tax incentive package that was granted to industrial estate developers in Laguna and Cavite provinces, just south of Manila.
In the past years, developers of industrial estates were given income tax holiday and preferential tariff rate on imported equipment.
The Philippines' Board of Investments has excluded Laguna and Cavite from this year's list of provinces eligible for tax incentives to encourage developers to develop industrial estates elsewhere.
Earlier, URDI had said it would allot 2.5 billion pesos to transform a sprawling agricultural land owned by the provincial government into an industrial site.
URDI manager Joel Adriano said the alloted funds would be diverted instead to a residential project in the hillside resort city of Tagaytay.
